E1.evidence: The reporter (humble, source build with -fsanitize=thread, FastRTPS) posts two ThreadSanitizer reports and a reproducer ("we can also run test_graph__rmw_fastrtps_cpp within the build/rcl_action"); a maintainer confirms: "It's a potential dead-lock." and lists the lock sequence in rmw_fastrtps (https://github.com/ros2/ros2/issues/1488#issuecomment-1752278901).

E2.evidence: Both documented defects are inside one unit's own logic. (1) The lock-order inversion is between two mutexes that rmw_fastrtps_cpp itself acquires in opposite orders: rmw_create_client holds "std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lck(participant_info->entity_creation_mutex_);" and then takes "std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(common_context->node_update_mutex);", while rmw_create_subscription holds node_update_mutex and, on its error path, calls rmw_fastrtps_shared_cpp::destroy_subscription, which takes entity_creation_mutex_. node_update_mutex is a public member of rmw_dds_common::Context, but rmw_dds_common takes no part in the ordering; the inversion would occur with any correct rmw_dds_common (and with any correct caller such as rcl_action). (2) The data race is between two threads inside Fast-DDS's FlowControllerImpl.hpp ("accessing the change->writer_info.previous or change->writer_info.next in T16(mutexes: write M18210) and T37(mutexes: write M18120, write M18121) is not protected by one same mutex"), internal to Fast-DDS.

E3.evidence: Observed while running rcl_action's test_graph__rmw_fastrtps_cpp (client and subscription creation on one context); not evaluated further because E2 fails.

E4.evidence: Two ThreadSanitizer reports are posted (https://pastebin.com/FdGR9iC1, https://pastebin.com/958rTvtB) and the lock-order-inversion log is reproduced in rmw_fastrtps PR #725; no hang is reported.

notes: The reporter lists two TSAN findings with equal weight. The packet's fix (rmw_fastrtps#725, "avoid using dds common public mutex directly", merged to rolling 2023-11-03 as d518e060) together with rmw_dds_common#73 ("make a new private mutex and add updating graph methods", 2273f384) and the rmw_cyclonedds#474 / rmw_connextdds#134 counterparts address only the lock-order inversion, by moving the graph update behind new rmw_dds_common::Context methods (add_publisher_graph, add_subscriber_graph, add_client_graph, add_service_graph) with a private mutex. That refactoring changes the rmw_dds_common API that the rmw implementations call, but the defect it removes is rmw_fastrtps_cpp's own inconsistent lock order, so I classify the case as internal at E2 step 2. The Fast-DDS FlowControllerImpl data race is not addressed by the linked PRs and is also internal (to Fast-DDS). A maintainer notes further unexamined TSAN warnings ("there are another TSAN warnings(not checked yet)").
